title: Three Shifts and One Short Rope
subtitle: 习惯自律 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）
meta: 主题语境：习惯自律（生活与学习·良好习惯与自律）　|　核心词汇：schedule　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 schedule 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the foreman ① made the schedule that no worker in the site would have counted, and he said the making was the whole of the shift. The ② schedule, meaning the timetable itself and not the rope, ran three shifts and stayed uncounted in the book; a schedule, he said, is the only thing in a site that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ schedule in that site had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ schedule at the far ramp, meaning the load they kept for the children to lift and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A schedule, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the foreman said the counting is the part that fills three shifts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the schedule was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the timetable. The ⑥ schedule, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; schedule, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a timetable and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ schedule had become a line in a sheet, and the sheet had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ schedule of the whole thing, the foreman wrote in May, was one site and three shifts of counting; schedule, he said, is either the load at the far ramp or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ schedule I remember is the timetable counted in the sheet, which closed in 1962 and is still counted as the quietest in the site. A ⑩ schedule, my mother said in 1964, is the only timetable that improves by being counted; every schedule, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a timetable. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 日程；时间表（指工地里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 日程；时间表（指那份日程本身，与短短的绳索相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the schedule 排这一份日程
D. n. 日程；时间表（指留给孩子们抬的那一车）
E. n. 日程之事（抽象总称，指一处工地的日程之事）
F. n. 日程；时间表（指施工单里写到、被清点的那一份）
G. n. 日程、条理（指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 条理（抽象总称，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the schedule that no worker in the site would have counted

answers.why: make the schedule 意为“排这一份日程”，1955 年那位工头把工地里没有一位工人肯清点的一份日程做了一遍。
schedule 意为“日程；时间表”，指那份日程本身而不是短短的绳索，它经过了三个班次而在簿子上没有被清点。
schedule 意为“日程；时间表”，指工地里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一根短短的绳索。
schedule 意为“日程；时间表”，指最远那道坡台的留给孩子们抬的那一车，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
schedule 意为“日程、条理”，指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份条理就是那件事的全部。
schedule 意为“条理”，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份日程，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
schedule 意为“日程；时间表”，指施工单里写到、被清点的那一份，到 1960 年这一份成了施工单里的一行。
schedule 意为“日程之事”，工头五月写道，整件事的日程之事是一处工地和三个班次的清点。
schedule 意为“日程；时间表”，我记得的是施工单里清点过的那一份，1962 年收工了，至今仍被说成工地里最安静的一份。
schedule 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，日程是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的日程。
